buying.title: Buying Property on Pelješac, Croatia
buying.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to property acquisition, legal checks, taxes, and purchase costs.
buying.introStatement: EU citizens buy property in Croatia under the exact same conditions as Croatian citizens.
buying.introBody: Foreign buyers often fear navigating unfamiliar real estate laws and language barriers. Sottomonte guarantees complete transparency: title searches, permit checks, and attorney-backed contracts.

processSteps.title: Initial consultation
processSteps.body: We analyze your criteria and propose matching Pelješac properties, including off-market options.

processSteps.title: Property viewings
processSteps.body: We inspect properties together without pressure, detailing location advantages, infrastructure, and investment ROI.

processSteps.title: Legal document check
processSteps.body: Before any deposit, our legal team verifies title deeds, land registry entries, encumbrances, and building permits.

processSteps.title: Contract and notarization
processSteps.body: An attorney drafts a bilingual contract. Signatures are certified by a notary, with power of attorney support available.

processSteps.title: Tax filing, title registration, handover
processSteps.body: We handle the real estate transfer tax declaration, land registry submission, and official key handover.

buying.costsIntro: In addition to the agreed purchase price, expect additional purchase costs in Croatia of roughly 4% to 5%:

costs.label: Real estate transfer tax
costs.note: One-time payment after acquisition. Exempt for new developments where VAT is included in the price.

costs.label: Notary and land registry fees
costs.note: Fees for signature notarization and land registry court submission fees.

costs.label: Lawyer
costs.note: Not mandatory, but we recommend one. We work with trusted lawyers who speak your language.

costs.label: Agency commission
costs.note: Agreed transparently and up front, before the first viewing.

faq.question: Can I buy property in Croatia as a foreigner?
faq.answer: EU citizens buy without any restrictions, exactly like Croatian citizens. Non-EU citizens need consent from the Ministry of Justice based on reciprocity, or buy through a Croatian company. We guide you through either route.

faq.question: What are the total costs on top of the price?
faq.answer: Roughly 4 to 5% extra: the 3% transfer tax, notary and land registry fees, and a lawyer. The agency commission is agreed up front, before the first viewing.

faq.question: How long does buying take?
faq.answer: From agreement to signing usually takes two to four weeks, and with tax and registration the whole process takes four to eight weeks. You normally receive the keys right after payment.

faq.question: Do I need to be in Croatia to buy?
faq.answer: No. With a power of attorney certified by a notary or at a Croatian consulate, we can complete the entire process without you travelling.

faq.question: What do you check before a purchase?
faq.answer: Clean 1/1 ownership, liens and mortgages, cadastre and land registry alignment, and building and usage permits. If something is not clean, you will hear it from us, before the offer.

faq.question: Can I rent the property out to tourists?
faq.answer: Yes, with a categorization permit. The procedure is standard and we help you start it after the purchase.
